gap: No result ChatGPT got states price per kWh. At the makers' own stores on 2026-11-13, BLUETTI Apex 300 + B300K cost $2,599 for 5,529.6 Wh ($470/kWh). ChatGPT's Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus card said $3,149, but the store price is $3,499 for 5,040 Wh ($694/kWh), sold out with pre-orders shipping Nov 28. ChatGPT's $2,999.99 Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus shows Sold Out on ankersolix.com.
standout_why: I checked the cited itechguides buying guide and sizing guide, outagereadyhq, and calcpanel. itechguides lists prices only for small stations (Explorer 1000 v2 at $559, S2000 at $699.99) and for the $6,199 DELTA Pro Ultra 12 kWh, with no $/kWh. outagereadyhq has transfer-switch prices plus 5000 Plus at $3,499, S5000 at $2,599.99 and TITAN 5000 'from $2,499', but no $/kWh, no BLUETTI and no stock status. calcpanel names no products or prices. None of them compares price per kWh across the 3–5.5 kWh home-backup tier, and none flags that two of ChatGPT's three cards are sold out or priced differently today.
decides: This works against ChatGPT's cards. Of its three picks, the F3800 Plus can't be bought from Anker today, and the 5000 Plus costs $350 more than the card said and ships Nov 28. Our BLUETTI Apex 300 + B300K is in stock and gives about 32% more Wh per dollar than the 5000 Plus. The 5000 Plus is still the pick for 7,200 W of 120/240 V output or whole-home loads like central AC.
